paper.title_en: When the electrons go marching in: Resonances and accuracy of pairwise approximations in multiterminal Josephson junctions
paper.abstract_en: Multiterminal Josephson junctions connect three or more superconductors through a common weak link. We quantify when their equilibrium currents admit a pairwise description. Multiterminal irreducible harmonics are energy components that depend jointly on three or more terminal phases and cannot be reduced to a sum of pair couplings. In microscopic planar-junction models, pairwise terms can capture nearly all energy variation while leaving appreciable current errors: phase differentiation amplifies the omitted harmonics. A terminal-independent Fourier projection quantifies this effect while allowing arbitrary nonsinusoidal pair couplings. Shared normal-region resonances provide a means of controlling the error. Selecting a mode from normal-state data and shifting it with a gate while retaining a frozen background reproduces the normalized error trends in the tested devices; prediction of the complete current waveform also depends on the background contribution. Finite-gap calculations retain the gate dependence at substantially lower absolute currents. An analytic single-level model supplies a sufficient detuning for pairwise accuracy. Together, these results connect normal-resonance control to a quantitative, current-based criterion for pairwise modeling.
